sanskrit: tam eva śāstrakartāraṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ niṣṭhāṃ nārāyaṇam ṛṣiṃ nānyo 'stīti ca vādinaḥ
english: Him alone the wise declare to be the author of the scriptures, and they proclaim that the seer Nārāyaṇa is the final ground, that no other exists beside him.

sanskrit: niḥsaṃśayeṣu sarveṣu nityaṃ vasati vai hariḥ sasaṃśayān hetubalān nādhyāvasati mādhavaḥ
english: In all those who are free of doubt Hari dwells forever; but in those still beset by doubt, who lean upon mere argument, Mādhava does not abide.

sanskrit: pañcarātravido ye tu yathākramaparā nṛpa ekāntabhāvopagatās te hariṃ praviśanti vai
english: But those, O king, who know the Pañcarātra and follow its order step by step, who have attained single-minded devotion—they truly enter into Hari.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca sanātane dve; vedāś ca sarve nikhilena rājan sarvaiḥ samastair ṛṣibhir nirukto; nārāyaṇo viśvam idaṃ purāṇam
english: Sāṃkhya and Yoga are the two eternal paths, O king, and the Vedas entire in all their fullness; by all the seers together it has been declared that Nārāyaṇa is this whole ancient universe.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhaṃ karma samīritaṃ yat; pravartate sarvalokeṣu kiṃ cit tasmād ṛṣes tad bhavatīti vidyād; divy antarikṣe bhuvi cāpsu cāpi
english: Whatever deed, good or evil, is set in motion and proceeds in all the worlds—let it be known that it issues from that seer alone, whether in heaven, in the mid-air, on earth, or in the waters.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca bahavaḥ puruṣā brahmann utāho eka eva tu ko hy atra puruṣaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ ko vā yonir ihocyate
english: Janamejaya said: Are the puruṣas many, O brahmin, or is there but one? Who here is the supreme Puruṣa, and what is said to be the source in this matter?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bahavaḥ puruṣā loke sāṃkhyayogavicāriṇām naitad icchanti puruṣam ekaṃ kurukulodvaha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: For those who reason after the manner of Sāṃkhya and Yoga the puruṣas in the world are many; these do not hold that the Puruṣa is one, O upholder of the Kuru line.

sanskrit: bahūnāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ ca yathaikā yonir ucyate tathā taṃ puruṣaṃ viśvaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi guṇādhikam
english: But just as a single source is spoken of for the many puruṣas, so shall I expound that all-pervading Puruṣa who transcends the strands of nature.

sanskrit: namaskṛtvā tu gurave vyāsāyāmitatejase tapoyuktāya dāntāya vandyāya paramarṣaye
english: Having paid homage to the teacher Vyāsa of measureless splendour, devoted to austerity, self-controlled, worthy of worship, the supreme seer—

sanskrit: idaṃ puruṣasūktaṃ hi sarvavedeṣu pārthiva ṛtaṃ satyaṃ ca vikhyātam ṛṣisiṃhena cintitam
english: This Hymn of the Puruṣa, O lord of the earth, is renowned in all the Vedas as the cosmic order and as truth, pondered by that lion among seers.

sanskrit: utsargeṇāpavādena ṛṣibhiḥ kapilādibhiḥ adhyātmacintām āśritya śāstrāṇy uktāni bhārata
english: By way of general rule and exception, the seers led by Kapila, taking their stand on inquiry into the inner Self, have set forth the scriptures, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: samāsatas tu yad vyāsaḥ puruṣaikatvam uktavān tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi prasādād amitaujasaḥ
english: In brief I shall declare to you, by the grace of that one of boundless might, the unity of the Puruṣa even as Vyāsa has proclaimed it.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam brahmaṇā saha saṃvādaṃ tryambakasya viśāṃ pate
english: On this point too they recite this ancient tale, the dialogue between the three-eyed god and Brahmā, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: kṣīrodasya samudrasya madhye hāṭakasaprabhaḥ vaijayanta iti khyātaḥ parvatapravaro nṛpa
english: In the midst of the Ocean of Milk there stands, gleaming like gold, the foremost of mountains renowned as Vaijayanta, O king.

sanskrit: tatrādhyātmagatiṃ deva ekākī pravicintayan vairājasadane nityaṃ vaijayantaṃ niṣevate
english: There the god, dwelling alone and meditating upon the course of the inner Self, ever frequents Vaijayanta from his abode of Virāj.

sanskrit: atha tatrāsatas tasya caturvaktrasya dhīmataḥ lalāṭaprabhavaḥ putraḥ śiva āgād yadṛcchayā ākāśenaiva yogīśaḥ purā trinayanaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Now as that wise four-faced one sat there, his son Śiva, born from his brow, came of his own accord—long ago, the lord of yogins, the three-eyed master, gliding through the very sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ khān nipapātāśu dharaṇīdharamūrdhani agrataś cābhavat prīto vavande cāpi pādayoḥ
english: Then he descended swiftly from the heavens upon the summit of that mountain, and stood before him well pleased, and bowed at his feet.

sanskrit: taṃ pādayor nipatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā savyena pāṇinā utthāpayām āsa tadā prabhur ekaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: Seeing him fallen at his feet, the lord, the sole Prajāpati, then raised him up with his left hand.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ bhagavāṃś cirasyāgatam ātmajam svāgataṃ te mahābāho diṣṭyā prāpto 'si me 'ntikam
english: And the Blessed One spoke to his son, come after so long: "Welcome to you, mighty-armed one; by good fortune you have come into my presence."

sanskrit: kaccit te kuśalaṃ putra svādhyāyatapasoḥ sadā nityam ugratapās tvaṃ hi tataḥ pṛcchāmi te punaḥ
english: "Is it well with you, my son, in your study and your austerity always? For you are ever fierce in penance—therefore I ask you again."

sanskrit: rudra uvāca tvatprasādena bhagavan svādhyāyatapasor mama kuśalaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva sarvasya jagatas tathā
english: Rudra said: By your grace, Blessed One, it is well and undiminished with me in study and austerity, and so it is with the whole world.

sanskrit: ciradṛṣṭo hi bhagavān vairājasadane mayā tato 'haṃ parvataṃ prāptas tv imaṃ tvatpādasevitam
english: Long had I not beheld you, Blessed One, in your abode of Virāj; therefore have I come to this mountain that is hallowed by the service of your feet.

sanskrit: kautūhalaṃ cāpi hi me ekāntagamanena te naitat kāraṇam alpaṃ hi bhaviṣyati pitāmaha
english: And I am moved with wonder at your going apart into solitude; for the cause of this can be no small one, O grandsire.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tat sadanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kṣutpipāsāvivarjitam surāsurair adhyuṣitam ṛṣibhiś cāmitaprabhaiḥ
english: What of that supreme dwelling, free from hunger and thirst, inhabited by gods and demons and by seers of measureless lustre—

sanskrit: gandharvair apsarobhiś ca satataṃ saṃniṣevitam utsṛjyemaṃ girivaram ekākī prāptavān asi
english: —forever frequented by gandharvas and apsarases, that you have forsaken to come alone to this best of mountains?

sanskrit: brahmovāca vaijayanto girivaraḥ satataṃ sevyate mayā atraikāgreṇa manasā puruṣaś cintyate virāṭ
english: Brahmā said: This best of mountains, Vaijayanta, is ever frequented by me; here, with mind one-pointed, the cosmic Puruṣa, Virāṭ, is meditated upon.

sanskrit: rudra uvāca bahavaḥ puruṣā brahmaṃs tvayā sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā sṛjyante cāpare brahman sa caikaḥ puruṣo virāṭ
english: Rudra said: Many puruṣas, O Brahmā, have been created by you the Self-born, and others, O Brahmā, are being created—yet that Puruṣa, Virāṭ, is one.

sanskrit: ko hy asau cintyate brahmaṃs tvayā vai puruṣottamaḥ etan me saṃśayaṃ brūhi mahat kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: Who then is he, O Brahmā, the Supreme Puruṣa upon whom you meditate? Resolve me this doubt, for great is my wonder.

sanskrit: brahmovāca bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ putra ye tvayā samudāhṛtāḥ evam etad atikrāntaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ naivam ity api ādhāraṃ tu pravakṣyāmi ekasya puruṣasya te
english: Brahmā said: The many puruṣas you have named, my son—this view, though it goes past the mark, is yet to be regarded, and so is the view that it is not so; but I shall declare to you the ground of the one Puruṣa.

sanskrit: bahūnāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ sa yathaikā yonir ucyate tathā taṃ puruṣaṃ viśvaṃ paramaṃ sumahattamam nirguṇaṃ nirguṇā bhūtvā praviśanti sanātanam
english: As a single source is spoken of for the many puruṣas, so into that all-pervading Puruṣa, supreme and greatest of the great, free of all qualities, men become free of qualities and enter—the eternal one.

sanskrit: brahmovāca śṛṇu putra yathā hy eṣa puruṣaḥ śāśvato 'vyayaḥ akṣayaś cāprameyaś ca sarvagaś ca nirucyate
english: Brahmā said: Hear, my son, how this Puruṣa is declared to be everlasting and imperishable, undecaying, immeasurable, and all-pervading.

sanskrit: na sa śakyas tvayā draṣṭuṃ mayānyair vāpi sattama saguṇo nirguṇo viśvo jñānadṛśyo hy asau smṛtaḥ
english: He cannot be seen by you, nor by me, nor by any other, O best one; with qualities yet without qualities, all-pervading, he is remembered to be visible only to knowledge.

sanskrit: aśarīraḥ śarīreṣu sarveṣu nivasaty asau vasann api śarīreṣu na sa lipyati karmabhiḥ
english: Bodiless, he dwells within all bodies; and though he dwells within bodies, he is not stained by their deeds.

sanskrit: mamāntarātmā tava ca ye cānye dehasaṃjñitāḥ sarveṣāṃ sākṣibhūto 'sau na grāhyaḥ kena cit kva cit
english: He is the inner Self of me and of you and of all others who bear the name of body; the witness of them all, he cannot be grasped by anyone anywhere.

sanskrit: viśvamūrdhā viśvabhujo viśvapādākṣināsikaḥ ekaś carati kṣetreṣu svairacārī yathāsukham
english: His head is all heads, his arms all arms, his feet, eyes, and nostrils all of these; alone he moves through the fields, ranging at will and at his ease.

sanskrit: kṣetrāṇi hi śarīrāṇi bījāni ca śubhāśubhe tāni vetti sa yogātmā tataḥ kṣetrajña ucyate
english: The fields are the bodies, and the seeds are the good and evil deeds; these he, whose essence is yoga, knows—therefore is he called the Knower of the Field.

sanskrit: nāgatir na gatis tasya jñeyā bhūtena kena cit sāṃkhyena vidhinā caiva yogena ca yathākramam
english: Neither his coming nor his going can be known by any being, neither by the method of Sāṃkhya nor by Yoga, however step by step pursued.

sanskrit: cintayāmi gatiṃ cāsya na gatiṃ vedmi cottamām yathājñānaṃ tu vakṣyāmi puruṣaṃ taṃ sanātanam
english: I ponder his course, yet I do not know that supreme course; but as far as my knowledge reaches I shall speak of that eternal Puruṣa.

sanskrit: tasyaikatvaṃ mahattvaṃ hi sa caikaḥ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ mahāpuruṣaśabdaṃ sa bibharty ekaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: His is oneness and greatness, and he is remembered as the one Puruṣa; he alone, the eternal one, bears the name Great Puruṣa.

sanskrit: eko hutāśo bahudhā samidhyate; ekaḥ sūryas tapasāṃ yonir ekā eko vāyur bahudhā vāti loke; mahodadhiś cāmbhasāṃ yonir ekaḥ puruṣaś caiko nirguṇo viśvarūpas; taṃ nirguṇaṃ puruṣaṃ cāviśanti
english: One fire is kindled in manifold ways; one is the sun, and one the source of all heats; one wind blows in many ways through the world; the great ocean is the one source of all waters; and one is the Puruṣa, without qualities, of universal form—into that quality-less Puruṣa men enter.

sanskrit: hitvā guṇamayaṃ sarvaṃ karma hitvā śubhāśubham ubhe satyānṛte tyaktvā evaṃ bhavati nirguṇaḥ
english: Forsaking all that is made of the qualities, abandoning deeds good and evil, casting off both truth and untruth—thus one becomes free of qualities.

sanskrit: acintyaṃ cāpi taṃ jñātvā bhāvasūkṣmaṃ catuṣṭayam vicared yo yatir yattaḥ sa gacchet puruṣaṃ prabhum
english: And the ascetic who, having known that unthinkable fourfold subtlety of being, ranges ever vigilant—he shall attain the lordly Puruṣa.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi paramātmānaṃ ke cid icchanti paṇḍitāḥ ekātmānaṃ tathātmānam apare 'dhyātmacintakāḥ
english: Thus some learned men hold him to be the Supreme Self; others, the inquirers into the inner Self, hold him to be the one Self, and the Self of all.

sanskrit: tatra yaḥ paramātmā hi sa nityaṃ nirguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ sa hi nārāyaṇo jñeyaḥ sarvātmā puruṣo hi saḥ na lipyate phalaiś cāpi padmapatram ivāmbhasā
english: Among these, he who is the Supreme Self is remembered as eternally free of qualities; he is to be known as Nārāyaṇa, the Self of all, the very Puruṣa; nor is he stained by the fruits of deeds, as the lotus-leaf is untouched by the water.

sanskrit: karmātmā tv aparo yo 'sau mokṣabandhaiḥ sa yujyate sasaptadaśakenāpi rāśinā yujyate hi saḥ evaṃ bahuvidhaḥ proktaḥ puruṣas te yathākramam
english: But that other, whose essence is action, is bound up with bondage and release; he is joined too with the aggregate of seventeen and one. Thus has the Puruṣa been declared to you in manifold ways, in due order.

sanskrit: yat tat kṛtsnaṃ lokatantrasya dhāma; vedyaṃ paraṃ bodhanīyaṃ saboddhṛ mantā mantavyaṃ prāśitā prāśitavyaṃ; ghrātā ghreyaṃ sparśitā sparśanīyam
english: That which is the whole abode of the world's fabric, the supreme to be known, to be awakened to, together with the awakener—he is the thinker and the thing thought, the taster and the thing to be tasted, the smeller and the thing to be smelt, the toucher and the thing to be touched;

sanskrit: draṣṭā draṣṭavyaṃ śrāvitā śrāvaṇīyaṃ; jñātā jñeyaṃ saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ ca yad vai proktaṃ guṇasāmyaṃ pradhānaṃ; nityaṃ caitac chāśvataṃ cāvyayaṃ ca
english: —the seer and the thing seen, the hearer and the thing to be heard, the knower and the thing known, with qualities and without; that which is declared to be the equipoise of the strands, the Primordial Nature—this is eternal, everlasting, and imperishable.

sanskrit: yad vai sūte dhātur ādyaṃ nidhānaṃ; tad vai viprāḥ pravadante 'niruddham yad vai loke vaidikaṃ karma sādhu; āśīryuktaṃ tad dhi tasyopabhojyam
english: That which the Ordainer first brings forth, the primal treasure-house, the brahmins call Aniruddha; and whatever Vedic rite is rightly performed in the world, joined with its blessing, is indeed his to enjoy.

sanskrit: devāḥ sarve munayaḥ sādhu dāntās; taṃ prāg yajñair yajñabhāgaṃ yajante ahaṃ brahmā ādya īśaḥ prajānāṃ; tasmāj jātas tvaṃ ca mattaḥ prasūtaḥ matto jagaj jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ ca; sarve vedāḥ sarahasyā hi putra
english: All the gods and the well-disciplined sages worship him first with sacrifices as the receiver of the sacrificial share. I am Brahmā, the first lord of creatures; from him am I born, and you from me; from me the world, moving and unmoving, and all the Vedas with their secret lore, O son.

sanskrit: caturvibhaktaḥ puruṣaḥ sa krīḍati yathecchati evaṃ sa eva bhagavāñ jñānena pratibodhitaḥ
english: Divided fourfold, that Puruṣa sports as he wills; thus is the Blessed One himself awakened to through knowledge.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ putra yathāvad anupṛcchataḥ sāṃkhyajñāne tathā yoge yathāvad anuvarṇitam
english: This has been told to you, my son, as you asked, in due form, and described as it is both in the knowledge of Sāṃkhya and in Yoga.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dharmāḥ pitāmahenoktā mokṣadharmāśritāḥ śubhāḥ dharmam āśramiṇāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vaktum arhati me bhavān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The auspicious duties grounded in the law of liberation have been declared by the grandsire; now may you tell me the highest duty of those who dwell in the orders of life.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarvatra vihito dharmaḥ svargyaḥ satyaphalodayaḥ bahudvārasya dharmasya nehāsti viphalā kriyā
english: Bhīṣma said: Everywhere duty is ordained that leads to heaven and yields the fruit of truth; of duty, which has many doors, no act here is barren.

sanskrit: yasmin yasmiṃs tu viṣaye yo yo yāti viniścayam sa tam evābhijānāti nānyaṃ bharatasattama
english: But in whatever sphere a man arrives at his settled conviction, that alone he comes to know, and no other, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: api ca tvaṃ naravyāghra śrotum arhasi me kathām purā śakrasya kathitāṃ nāradena surarṣiṇā
english: And moreover, O tiger among men, you should hear from me a tale told long ago to Śakra by the divine seer Nārada.

sanskrit: surarṣir nārado rājan siddhas trailokyasaṃmataḥ paryeti kramaśo lokān vāyur avyāhato yathā
english: The divine seer Nārada, O king, a perfected one honoured throughout the three worlds, ranges in turn through the worlds, like the wind that none can obstruct.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin maheṣvāsa devarājālayaṃ gataḥ satkṛtaś ca mahendreṇa pratyāsannagato 'bhavat
english: Once, O mighty archer, he went to the abode of the king of the gods, and being honoured by great Indra, he came and seated himself near at hand.

sanskrit: taṃ kṛtakṣaṇam āsīnaṃ paryapṛcchac chacīpatiḥ brahmarṣe kiṃ cid āścaryam asti dṛṣṭaṃ tvayānagha
english: As he sat there at his ease, the lord of Śacī questioned him: "O brahmin-seer, is there any wonder that you have seen, O sinless one?

sanskrit: yathā tvam api viprarṣe trailokyaṃ sacarācaram jātakautūhalo nityaṃ siddhaś carasi sākṣivat
english: "For you, O brahmin-seer, ever moved by curiosity, range as a perfected one through the three worlds with all that moves and is still, like a witness."

sanskrit: na hy asty aviditaṃ loke devarṣe tava kiṃ cana śrutaṃ vāpy anubhūtaṃ vā dṛṣṭaṃ vā kathayasva me
english: "For there is nothing in the world unknown to you, O divine seer; tell me, then, whatever you have heard, or experienced, or seen."

sanskrit: tasmai rājan surendrāya nārado vadatāṃ varaḥ āsīnāyopapannāya proktavān vipulāṃ kathām
english: To that king of the gods, O king, as he sat and made his fitting request, Nārada, best of speakers, related a far-reaching tale.

sanskrit: yathā yena ca kalpena sa tasmai dvijasattamaḥ kathāṃ kathitavān pṛṣṭas tathā tvam api me śṛṇu
english: In what manner and by what fashion that best of the twice-born, being asked, told him the tale—even so do you now hear it from me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca āsīt kila kuruśreṣṭha mahāpadme purottame gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe tīre kaś cid vipraḥ samāhitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: There was once, O best of the Kurus, in the noblest of cities, Mahāpadma, upon the southern bank of the Gaṅgā, a certain brahmin of composed mind.

sanskrit: saumyaḥ somānvaye vede gatādhvā chinnasaṃśayaḥ dharmanityo jitakrodho nityatṛpto jitendriyaḥ
english: Gentle, of the lineage of Soma, accomplished in the Veda's course, with all doubts severed, ever devoted to duty, master of his anger, ever content, his senses subdued—

sanskrit: ahiṃsānirato nityaṃ satyaḥ sajjanasaṃmataḥ nyāyaprāptena vittena svena śīlena cānvitaḥ
english: —ever delighting in non-harming, truthful, honoured by the good, endowed with wealth rightfully gained and with his own virtuous conduct;

sanskrit: jñātisaṃbandhivipule mitrāpāśrayasaṃmate kule mahati vikhyāte viśiṣṭāṃ vṛttim āsthitaḥ
english: In a great and renowned family, rich in kinsmen and connections, esteemed as a refuge by its friends, he kept to a distinguished course of life.

sanskrit: sa putrān bahulān dṛṣṭvā vipule karmaṇi sthitaḥ kuladharmāśrito rājan dharmacaryāparo 'bhavat
english: Seeing his many sons, established in his abundant rites, abiding by the duty of his line, O king, he became wholly devoted to the practice of dharma.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa dharmaṃ vedoktaṃ yathāśāstroktam eva ca śiṣṭācīrṇaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca trividhaṃ cintya cetasā
english: Then, pondering in his mind the threefold dharma—that declared in the Veda, that declared in the treatises, and that practised by the cultured—

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me syāc chubhaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ kṣamaṃ kiṃ parāyaṇam ity evaṃ khidyate nityaṃ na ca yāti viniścayam
english: "What good might come to me from acting? What is fitting? What is the highest refuge?" Thus he was ever troubled, yet came to no certainty.

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ khidyamānasya dharmaṃ paramam āsthitaḥ kadā cid atithiḥ prāpto brāhmaṇaḥ susamāhitaḥ
english: As he was thus troubled, while abiding in the highest dharma, there came on a certain day a guest, a brahmin of well-composed mind.

sanskrit: sa tasmai satkriyāṃ cakre kriyāyuktena hetunā viśrāntaṃ cainam āsīnam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He showed him hospitality with the rite due to such an occasion, and when the guest had rested and was seated, he spoke to him these words.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca samutpannābhidhāno 'smi vāṅmādhuryeṇa te 'nagha mitratām abhipannas tvāṃ kiṃ cid vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: The brahmin said: A bond of name has arisen between us through the sweetness of your speech, O sinless one; having come to friendship with you, I shall say something to you—hear it.

sanskrit: gṛhasthadharmaṃ viprendra kṛtvā putragataṃ tv aham dharmaṃ paramakaṃ kuryāṃ ko hi mārgo bhaved dvija
english: Having fulfilled the householder's duty, O lord of brahmins, and that which concerns my sons, I would now perform the highest dharma; what then, O brahmin, should be my path?

sanskrit: aham ātmānam ātmastham eka evātmani sthitaḥ kartuṃ kāṅkṣāmi necchāmi baddhaḥ sādhāraṇair guṇaiḥ
english: Standing alone within the Self, I long to make the Self abide in the Self; I no longer wish to be bound by the common strands of nature.

sanskrit: yāvad evānatītaṃ me vayaḥ putraphalāśritam tāvad icchāmi pātheyam ādātuṃ pāralaukikam
english: So long as the season of my life, given over to the fruit of sons, has not yet wholly passed, so long do I wish to gather provision for the world beyond.

sanskrit: asmin hi lokasaṃtāne paraṃ pāram abhīpsataḥ utpannā me matir iyaṃ kuto dharmamayaḥ plavaḥ
english: For in this unending stream of worldly existence, as I yearn for the farther shore, this thought has arisen in me: where is the raft made of dharma?

sanskrit: samuhyamānāni niśamya loke; niryātyamānāni ca sāttvikāni dṛṣṭvā ca dharmadhvajaketumālāṃ; prakīryamāṇām upari prajānām
english: Hearing how in the world good things are swept away and carried off, and seeing the garland of pennon and banner of dharma scattered above the heads of creatures—

sanskrit: na me mano rajyati bhogakāle; dṛṣṭvā yatīn prārthayataḥ paratra tenātithe buddhibalāśrayeṇa; dharmārthatattve viniyuṅkṣva māṃ tvam
english: —my mind takes no delight in the season of enjoyment, seeing the ascetics who strive after the world beyond. Therefore, O guest, with the support of your strength of understanding, set me to the truth of dharma and its purpose.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca so 'tithir vacanaṃ tasya śrutvā dharmābhilāṣiṇaḥ provāca vacanaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ prājño madhurayā girā
english: Bhīṣma said: That guest, hearing the words of the man who longed for dharma, being wise, spoke gentle words in a sweet voice.

sanskrit: aham apy atra muhyāmi mamāpy eṣa manorathaḥ na ca saṃniścayaṃ yāmi bahudvāre triviṣṭape
english: In this matter I too am bewildered; this same longing is mine as well, and I come to no certainty regarding heaven with its many doors.
